as.sfi_deduplication_instructions: Deduplicate Zambia Literacy and Language: English Language Lower Primary Grades 1-3 SFI candidates conservatively. The syllabus is organized by visible Grade headings, no-code Component headers such as Listening and Speaking, Reading, and Writing, then coded Topic, Sub-topic, and Specific Competence rows. For coded Topic, Sub-topic, and Specific Competence candidates, same statement_type plus same normalized official code is the primary merge signal and should normally merge when descriptions/source_text are compatible, especially when candidates come from adjacent overlapping table windows, repeated header/body rows, row-span/fill-down interpretation, continuation rows, or the same source segment/table row. Treat descriptions that differ only because one includes the leading code prefix and the other omits it as compatible. Do not merge candidates with different official codes solely because labels or skills are similar; different four-part Specific Competence codes should remain separate, including similar skills repeated across Grade 1, Grade 2, Grade 3, or different Components. The first numeric code component indicates grade context: 1.* = Grade 1, 2.* = Grade 2, and 3.* = Grade 3. Component candidates are no-code table-header groupings; labels such as Listening and Speaking, Reading, and Writing repeat across grades and overlapping windows. Merge duplicate Component candidates only when the same label is supported by the same grade/source segment/table header context or clear overlapping-window provenance; keep Component candidates separate across different grades or distinct source contexts. Merge Grade candidates only when they are clear duplicates of the same visible grade heading; keep Grade 1, Grade 2, and Grade 3 separate. Topic and Sub-topic labels may recur across grades or components; if their official codes differ, keep them separate. Treat duplicate buckets, repeated-text warnings, source segment overlap, and table row/header overlap as review signals only, not automatic merge rules. Choose conflict or needs_review when same-code candidates have materially incompatible descriptions/source context or when the bounded evidence is insufficient. Do not merge Learning Activities, Expected Standard descriptors, front matter, methodology, or Key Competences into SFIs.
as.sfi_extraction_instructions: Extract Zambia Literacy and Language StandardsFrameworkItem candidates from the English Language lower-primary syllabus tables. For this syllabus, the first numeric component of a code indicates the grade: 1.* = Grade 1, 2.* = Grade 2, and 3.* = Grade 3. Use the grade heading as grade context: Grade 1, Grade 2, or Grade 3. Treat Listening and Speaking, Reading, and Writing as component/strand grouping SFIs. In syllabus tables with columns Topic, Sub-topic, Specific Competences, Learning Activities, and Expected Standard, extract Topic and Sub-topic as Standard Grouping SFIs using their stable codes. Extract Specific Competences as the main leaf Standard SFIs and preserve the four-part statement_code. Treat Expected Standard as a descriptor or benchmark attached to the corresponding Specific Competence, not as a standalone Standard unless it is the only clear normative expectation in the row. Treat Learning Activities as guidance only, not SFIs. Do not extract Introduction, Structure of the Syllabus, Suggested Teaching Methodology, Time Allocation, Assessment, or Key Competences to be Developed as SFI candidates; treat them as front matter or auxiliary context only. Use rows_filldown for interpreting row-span context, but preserve raw row/cell text and provenance. Always retain page indices, table segment id, row order, source column, statement code, grade, component, topic, and sub-topic context.
as.sfi_has_child_instructions: Resolve Zambia Literacy and Language hasChild relationships conservatively using finalized SFIs only. The expected direct hierarchy for this source is StandardsFramework -> Grade -> Component -> Topic -> Sub-topic -> Specific Competence when those source-visible grouping SFIs exist. The only Component labels for this curriculum are Listening and Speaking, Reading, and Writing; they are no-code table-header groupings and they repeat separately for Grade 1, Grade 2, and Grade 3. The first numeric code component indicates grade context: 1.* = Grade 1, 2.* = Grade 2, and 3.* = Grade 3. Grade SFIs are direct children of the StandardsFramework root. Component SFIs are direct children of the matching Grade SFI for the same grade/source context. Topic SFIs are direct children of the matching Component SFI, not the Grade, when that same-grade Component endpoint is present in the child's parent_candidates list. For Topic children, identify the Component from the source table/component header: Topics in LISTENING AND SPEAKING belong under the same-grade Listening and Speaking Component; Topics in READING belong under the same-grade Reading Component; Topics in WRITING belong under the same-grade Writing Component. When choosing the parent for a Topic, prefer a same-grade Component candidate supported by the same source segment, extraction window, table header, or table context over any Grade candidate, even if the Grade candidate has matched_section_path_label, nearest_preceding_grouping, or statement_type_compatible evidence. Do not attach a Topic directly to a Grade unless no source-supported same-grade Component SFI is available in the supplied parent_candidates list. If the appropriate Component is absent from the supplied candidate set, choose the closest source-supported ancestor from the available candidates and explain that no direct Component candidate was supplied. Use code-parent hints only for coded hierarchy below Topic: Specific Competence -> Sub-topic and Sub-topic -> Topic. Do not use code-parent hints to skip the Component layer for Topic nodes; Topic codes identify grade and local topic identity, not a direct Grade parent. For Sub-topic children, select the finalized Topic whose normalized code matches the configured parent-code hint and whose source context is compatible. For Specific Competence children, select the finalized Sub-topic whose normalized code matches the configured parent-code hint and whose source context is compatible. DocumentIR section_path labels are evidence only and may contain stale cumulative headings from earlier pages or grades; do not let stale section_path labels override same-table/same-grade Component evidence. Repeated labels such as CONVERSATION, SOUNDS, HANDWRITING, SONGS, GAMES, Listening and Speaking, Reading, and Writing must remain separated by grade and source/table context. Do not choose parents by code alone, do not merge same-code/different-content endpoints, and do not add a StandardsFramework root parent when a direct semantic SFI parent is selected. Select the StandardsFramework root only for top-level Grade/grouping items or when no source-supported finalized SFI parent is available from the supplied candidates.

lc.generation_instructions: Create LearningComponents primarily from leaf Specific Competence SFIs. Use the source English text as-is. Prefer a 1-to-1 component when the competence is already atomic. Split only when one specific competence clearly contains multiple distinct language skills. Do not create LearningComponents from Topic or Sub-topic grouping nodes, Learning Activities, Expected Standard benchmarks, methodology prose, or the Key Competences table unless a later profile explicitly marks them as LC sources.
